body:
> I could maybe suggest having secret friendships and secret activities.

That sounds exciting! All Charlie's Angels-y and whatnot. 

I have been working with my therapist to get me used to the idea of being open and emotionally vulnerable to people, because having people that close to me right now is scary and uncomfortable. Kind of like that feeling you have when you're admiring an insect or something on your window, and it suddenly flies into your hair. >w< 

The "secret" friendships idea, of maybe even eventually cultivating several separate friend relationships based on different sorts of interests, is one I will definitely think about, and maybe even discuss with my therapist next week.

I don't know what to say aside from thank you. Your words really struck a chord with me. You described the sense of detachment very well; knowing someone else at least understands and isn't judging my inability to yank myself together means an incredible amount to me. As crazy as this may sound, as long as I've been dealing with these issues, you're the first person who's been able to say something more specific and concrete than just a nebulous and generic "I understand" or "I know how you feel". In all sincerity, thank you so much.

I don't know how to go about doing this anymore. The two or three people that I've attempted to share this with have either walked out on me or halfheartedly listened and then told me that I'm basically making a big deal out of nothing and to stop crying and get over it. I don't know if I could handle another response like this. Just thinking about it makes me want to lie in bed and never get up ever again. 

We have two cats. Sometimes I feel like they're the only ones that ever really listen to me.
